 AMES (KWWL) -- Iowa State athletic director Jared Benko announced a one-game suspension for long-time women's basketball coach Bill Fennelly on Sunday night.  The suspension came due to  inappropriate contact with a student-athlete during a timeout in the Cyclones' game against UIC. 
 Benko didn't name the player, however, Fennelly was seen making contact with the forehead of sophomore guard Sienna Harvey during a heated discussion in the Cyclones' huddle late in the second half. 
 "We cannot tolerate inappropriate contact between a coach or staff member and a student-athlete in practice or in competition, whether intentional or not," Benko said. "We have high expectations of all of our coaches, staff and student-athletes and we will not shy away from holding accountable those who fail to meet those expectations. I have met with Coach Fennelly and he has apologized to the student-athlete involved and regrets his actions."
 "I want to apologize to the student-athlete and her family, her teammates and all of Cyclone Nation for allowing my emotions to get the best of me during our game," Fennelly said. "I fully recognize that there are no situations where it is appropriate to make contact with a student-athlete in that way. I accept responsibility and will serve the suspension and I will do better moving forward." 
 Fennelly will serve the suspension on Wednesday when the team travels to Cedar Falls to face Northern Iowa.
